usage: Articles can also mean items or goods; sporting goods is more conventional for sports equipment.

definition: An arrangement for storing and organising materials on library shelves.
example: The librarian explained the stack system used to shelve journals.
usage: The phrase may have other technical meanings; this entry uses the library sense.

definition: A relatively simple initial project used to introduce a subject or skill.
example: Building a basic calculator is a useful starter project for programmers.

definition: The digestive organ that receives food and the organ that pumps blood.
example: The diagram identifies the stomach and heart.

definition: A storage building together with buildings used for religious worship.
example: The excavation plan marks a storehouse and temples.
usage: The phrase combines unrelated building types and is not a fixed expression.

definition: Methods used to reduce stress or cope with it.
example: The workshop teaches stress management through planning and relaxation.

definition: A smell that is powerful or easy to notice.
example: The flowers have a strong scent in the evening.

definition: Banking services or accounts designed for students.
example: The bank's student banking package includes an account with no monthly fee.

definition: A counter where students can obtain information.
example: Ask at the student information desk for a campus map.

definition: A service that helps students with academic or personal needs.
example: The student support service offers advice about financial difficulties.

definition: Methods used to learn and remember material effectively.
example: Testing yourself is one of the study techniques recommended by the tutor.

definition: A guide that helps users find information by subject.
example: The library's subject access guide lists databases for engineering research.
usage: This is a descriptive library phrase; its exact format depends on the institution.

definition: Enough specific information for a particular purpose.
example: Your application must include sufficient details about your work experience.

definition: The sun's apparent location in the sky.
example: The sun's position affects the length of a shadow.

definition: A survey has been carried out.
example: The survey conducted last spring included five hundred households.
usage: This is an incomplete passive or participial phrase; a full clause may be the survey was conducted.

definition: Swimming in water at or below a waterfall.
example: The photograph shows people swimming in a pool below a waterfall.
usage: Swimming at a waterfall or in a pool below a waterfall is clearer; the original does not specify the swimming location.

definition: To measure someone's body temperature.
example: The nurse took my temperature with a digital thermometer.

definition: Words and expressions used in a specialised field.
example: The course introduces the technical vocabulary of mechanical engineering.

definition: The amount of time spent providing lessons.
example: The course includes fifteen teaching hours each week.

definition: A document setting out the subjects and content to be taught.
example: The teaching syllabus lists the topics for each term.

definition: A dramatic story or series produced for television.
example: The television drama follows the lives of a family of doctors.

definition: The way a piece of writing is organised.
example: Understanding text structure helps readers follow an argument.

definition: People who have disabilities.
example: The building provides accessible facilities for people with disabilities.
usage: People with disabilities or disabled people is generally preferred to the collective label the disabled; individual preferences vary.

definition: The galaxy containing our solar system, seen from Earth as a pale band across the night sky.
example: We could see the Milky Way clearly from the dark campsite.

definition: The theories and concepts that provide a basis for a study or explanation.
example: The introduction explains the theoretical background to the experiment.

definition: Ideas explaining how a method or principle can be put into practice.
example: The seminar explored theories about applying the model in classrooms.
usage: This is not a widely fixed expression; theory and application or application of a theory may be intended, depending on context.

definition: The building level called the third floor.
example: The meeting room is on the third floor.
usage: In British usage this is normally three levels above the ground floor; American numbering often counts the ground level as the first floor.

definition: The process of determining how much time passes.
example: Accurate time measurement is essential in a sprint race.

definition: To a certain extent or amount.
example: The new timetable has reduced delays to some degree.

definition: Making physical contact with rocks.
example: The museum asks visitors to avoid touching rocks in the display.
usage: This is a literal action, not a fixed idiom.

definition: A factory that manufactures toys.
example: The toy factory produces wooden puzzles and model cars.

definition: The prevention of injuries and accidents involving road users.
example: The campaign teaches children about traffic safety.

definition: A prepaid cheque that travellers can exchange or use as payment, traditionally requiring their signature.
example: She kept a traveller's check separately from her cash.
usage: Traveller's cheque is the usual British spelling. These instruments are less common today.

definition: Money charged for instruction at a school, college or university.
example: The tuition fee is payable at the start of each term.

definition: Experiencing demands or stress that make a situation difficult.
example: She works well under pressure when deadlines are close.

definition: A way of eating that does not support good health.
example: An unhealthy diet may contain too much salt and too few vegetables.

definition: Buildings, equipment and services available at a university.
example: The university facilities include laboratories and a sports centre.

definition: A source of information, equipment or service available through a university.
example: The language laboratory is a university resource open to all students.

definition: A region characterised by a town or city and its developed surroundings.
example: Buses run more frequently in the urban area.

definition: To eat a wider range of foods or change what one usually eats.
example: Try to vary your diet by adding different vegetables each week.

definition: An electronic signal carrying moving-image information.
example: A loose cable interrupted the video signal to the monitor.

definition: Learning carried out through digital or online environments.
example: Virtual learning allows students to join lessons from home.

definition: A bath containing comfortably warm water.
example: She relaxed in a warm bath after the long walk.

definition: Shoes that can be cleaned by washing.
example: These washable shoes are useful for muddy outdoor activities.

definition: Making a blanket by interlacing threads.
example: She spent the afternoon weaving a blanket on a loom.
usage: Normally say weaving a blanket; woven blanket names the finished object.

definition: A return, report or yield calculated or submitted each week.
example: The branch submits a weekly return showing its sales figures.
usage: Return has several meanings; this entry uses the sense of a periodic report, which is unconfirmed without source context.

definition: A department responsible for social assistance or people's well-being.
example: The welfare department helped the family apply for support.

definition: To broaden one's knowledge, experience or understanding.
example: Travelling can widen your horizons by introducing you to different ways of life.
usage: The idiom normally uses the plural: widen your horizons or broaden your horizons.

definition: To take money out of a bank account in the form of notes or coins.
example: You can withdraw cash from the machine beside the bank.

definition: A specific result someone aims to achieve in their work.
example: My main work objective this month is to complete the customer survey.

definition: A large international exhibition where countries present achievements, ideas and culture.
example: The class discussed transport plans for a World Expo.
usage: Dates, locations and themes depend on the particular event.

definition: People without unusual status, power or special characteristics.
example: The exhibition shows how ordinary people lived a century ago.

definition: A quantity of something, usually something uncountable.
example: The amount of water in the tank has fallen.
usage: Often use the amount of or an amount of; use number of for countable items in careful writing.

definition: Once in each month or during each successive month.
example: I transfer money to my savings account every month.

definition: A body shape that is neither especially thin nor especially large.
example: The missing person is of medium build and has short hair.

definition: Hair that grows without curls or waves.
example: She has long straight hair that reaches her shoulders.

definition: Hair that is light in colour.
example: His fair hair became darker as he grew older.

definition: Long sections of hair woven into braids.
example: She wore her hair in two long plaits.

definition: A skirt decorated with alternating pink and white stripes.
example: The girl in the pink and white striped skirt is waiting near the gate.

definition: To be wearing red clothing.
example: The guide will be in red so you can recognise her.

definition: To have a necktie on as part of one's clothing.
example: Please wear a tie for the formal dinner.
usage: Normally say wear a tie, with an article.

definition: The address of the place where a person lives.
example: Write your home address on the application form.

definition: The date on which someone or something is registered.
example: The registration date appears at the top of the form.
usage: Registration date is the conventional noun phrase.

definition: The initial opinions or feelings someone has about a city.
example: My first impressions of the city were of busy streets and friendly people.

definition: A telephone number identifying a particular office.
example: Please write your office number on the visitor form.

definition: A centre that manages housing or accommodation for students.
example: The Student Accommodation Center handles room allocations.
usage: British institutions often spell centre; the official spelling may vary.

definition: Notices in newspapers promoting products, services, jobs or events.
example: She found the flat through newspaper advertisements.

definition: Areas outside towns and cities, usually with fewer people and buildings.
example: Rural areas often have fewer public transport services.

definition: A bedroom containing a bed for two people.
example: The flat has a double bedroom and a smaller study.

definition: A room used for storing goods or equipment.
example: Unused chairs are kept in the store room.
usage: Storeroom is also commonly written as one word.

definition: A long car hired to carry passengers, especially between an airport and a hotel.
example: The airport limousine collected us outside arrivals.

definition: To pay money as a punishment for breaking a law or rule.
example: You may have to pay a fine for parking here.

definition: Transport owned or arranged for private use rather than public service.
example: The conference venue is easier to reach by private transport.

definition: To verify that a booking or reservation is still wanted and valid.
example: Please confirm your reservation by email.

definition: To reserve a table at a restaurant.
example: We booked a table for four at seven o'clock.

definition: A flight taken after another flight, with a change between them.
example: Our connecting flight leaves from terminal two.
usage: Connecting flight is conventionally written as two words.

definition: An additional or excessive fee charged beyond the basic price.
example: The airline applied an excess charge for the heavy suitcase.

definition: The way seats are positioned or organised.
example: The theatre changed its seat arrangement for the lecture.

definition: The currency used in Japan.
example: The museum ticket costs 1,200 Japanese yen.
usage: Yen is usually lowercase when naming the currency; Japanese Yen may be a label or title.

definition: An area beside the sea or ocean.
example: The coastal area attracts visitors in summer.

definition: Some plants selected or referred to without specifying all of them.
example: Certain plants grow only in acidic soil.

definition: To give banknotes or coins in denominations of five.
example: Could you give me the money in fives, please?
usage: The wording is conversational; give me the money in five-pound notes is more explicit.

term: check the present balance in your account
definition: To look at how much money is currently in your bank account.
example: You can check the present balance in your account online.
usage: Current account balance is the more concise expression.

definition: The exchange value or price that applies now.
example: The current rate for euros is displayed on the screen.

definition: Advice that helps someone choose a career or occupation.
example: The college offers vocational guidance to final-year students.

definition: A person whose job involves entering information by pressing keys, historically on punched cards or a keyboard.
example: The key puncher entered the figures into the old accounting system.
usage: This is an old occupational term; data-entry clerk is more current.

definition: A doctor who specialises in diseases of the eyes.
example: The oculist examined my vision and prescribed new glasses.
usage: Oculist is an old-fashioned term; ophthalmologist or eye doctor is more current. Doctor is redundant in the original phrase.

definition: To be ill with a common viral infection causing a blocked or runny nose.
example: I have a cold, so I will stay home today.

definition: To feel slightly cold.
example: I began to feel chilly when the sun went down.

definition: A medicine or treatment intended to relieve a cold.
example: The pharmacist recommended a cold remedy for my sore throat.
usage: Cold remedy is the conventional phrase; cold cure is understandable but less common.

definition: To measure the pressure of blood flowing through the arteries.
example: The nurse took my blood pressure before the appointment.

definition: An industry that is especially important or successful in a region or economy.
example: Tourism is a leading industry in the coastal province.

definition: The average value calculated over a year.
example: The annual average rainfall is 800 millimetres.

definition: A temperature of twenty degrees below zero on the Celsius scale.
example: The overnight temperature fell to minus twenty degrees Celsius.

definition: The person, place or feature considered most interesting or important at an event.
example: The waterfall is the main attraction in the park.

definition: To be located a long distance from someone or something.
example: The village is far away from the nearest railway station.

definition: To travel directly toward a specified place.
example: Go straight to the reception desk when you arrive.

definition: To travel or point in a northern direction.
example: Continue along this road and go north for two kilometres.

definition: To be positioned on the left-hand side of another person.
example: The pharmacy is on your left.
usage: The source wording be on sb's left is a positional description; on someone's left is the usual form.

definition: Exactly on the opposite side or facing directly across from something.
example: The bank is directly opposite the post office.

definition: To be located at the meeting point of two edges or streets.
example: The café is in the corner of the square.
usage: Use at the corner of for streets; in the corner of is used for rooms or enclosed areas.

definition: A place where one road divides into two alternative roads.
example: At the fork in the road, take the left branch.
usage: A fork in the road is the conventional form.

definition: The northern part of the island of Ireland; commonly called Northern Ireland.
example: She is studying in Northern Ireland.
usage: North Ireland is not the usual official name; Northern Ireland is conventional.

definition: The organisation and ordering of courses in a programme.
example: The department published the course arrangement for next year.
usage: Course schedule or course structure may be more natural, depending on meaning.

definition: An object or resource used to help teach a lesson.
example: The teacher used a model as a teaching aid.

definition: Kept in a restricted collection or reserved storage area.
example: The requested book is held in the closed reserve.
usage: The original wording is malformed. In a library context, held in the closed reserve may be intended; without context, restricted storage is only an inferred meaning.

definition: A printer that applies coloured ink to paper.
example: The office replaced its old colour inkjet printer.
usage: The original has spelling errors: color inject printer is most reasonably colour inkjet printer. The exact device is inferred from the wording.

definition: Questions requiring answers of only a few words or a short sentence.
example: The test contains ten short-answer questions.
usage: Short-answer is conventionally hyphenated before a noun.

definition: Based on suitable data and statistical methods that justify the conclusions.
example: A representative sample helps produce statistically valid survey results.

definition: A rule controlling where, when or how vehicles may be parked.
example: The new parking regulation bans overnight parking on this street.

definition: An office that handles administrative tasks.
example: Submit the completed form to the admin office.
usage: Administrative office is more formal; admin office is common in speech.

definition: A large quantity or group of something.
example: A mass of paperwork arrived before the deadline.

definition: Many different kinds or varieties of something.
example: The market sells all sorts of handmade soap.

definition: A large number or group of people or things.
example: A host of volunteers helped clean the beach.

definition: A group of things that belong together or are used together.
example: The kit contains a set of tools for basic repairs.

definition: At the point or phase currently being discussed.
example: At this stage, we do not know the final cost.

definition: To be changed from one form, state or use into another.
example: The old warehouse was converted into apartments.

definition: To consist of particular parts or members.
example: The committee is made up of representatives from six departments.

definition: To be suddenly surprised or shocked.
example: I was taken aback by the unexpected price increase.

definition: To make up for a loss, disadvantage or cost.
example: The grant helps compensate for the reduced ticket income.

definition: To deliver or give a speech.
example: She will give the speech at the closing ceremony.
usage: Do the speech is nonstandard in this meaning; give or make a speech is conventional.

definition: To feel fear of someone or something.
example: Many children are afraid of thunder.

definition: To be expected or required to do something.
example: All applicants are expected to submit two references.

definition: To be exposed to or affected by something, often unpleasant.
example: The material was subjected to high temperatures during testing.

definition: To be accustomed to something.
example: I am used to working in a busy office.
usage: Follow be used to with a noun or -ing form, not a bare verb.

definition: To make journeys, usually for a particular purpose.
example: The engineer does regular trips to inspect remote sites.
usage: Make trips or take trips is more natural than do trips.

definition: By a much greater amount or degree.
example: This model is far more efficient than the old one.

definition: To board and leave a vehicle.
example: Passengers may get on and off the bus at any marked stop.

definition: To experience difficulty with someone or something.
example: I am having trouble with the online payment system.

definition: To contact or reach someone, especially after trying.
example: I finally got hold of the landlord by phone.

definition: To talk briefly with someone, often about a serious or private matter.
example: Could I have a word with you after the meeting?

definition: In general terms without giving many specific details.
example: In broad terms, the plan aims to reduce waste.

definition: During the busiest periods.
example: Travel costs rise in peak times.
usage: At peak times or during peak periods is more idiomatic than in peak times.

definition: To continue moving or working at a particular speed.
example: The runners kept up the pace until the final kilometre.

definition: To write something down so it will be remembered.
example: Make a note of the room number before you leave.

definition: Displayed or written on a board.
example: The exam timetable is on the board outside the office.

definition: To collect someone by vehicle or lift them from the ground.
example: I will pick you up at the station at six.

definition: To connect to a computer system or website.
example: Log on to the university portal with your student account.

definition: The brand and specific design of a product, especially a car or machine.
example: Please record the make and model of the damaged phone.
usage: Make and model is the conventional phrase; make model alone is incomplete.

definition: Dependence on someone or something for support or supply.
example: The region's reliance on imported fuel makes prices unstable.

definition: To use a period for a particular activity.
example: He spends time on research during the summer.

definition: To feel sympathy for someone and want to help them.
example: The nurse took pity on the exhausted traveller.

definition: To collect money for a purpose, often through donations or a campaign.
example: The students held a concert to raise money for the shelter.

definition: To remain relaxed and avoid panic.
example: Stay calm and follow the emergency instructions.

definition: The very large amount or quantity of something.
example: The sheer volume of applications overwhelmed the small admissions team.

definition: To receive a prize or honour for an achievement.
example: She won an award for her research on clean energy.

definition: To handle several tasks or responsibilities at the same time.
example: He juggles work with evening study.
usage: Juggle with can also mean physically tossing objects while keeping them in the air.

definition: A tour in which people visit places on foot.
example: We joined a walking tour of the historic centre.

definition: A passage used by players to enter or leave a sports field or court.
example: The teams lined up in the players' tunnel before the match.

definition: To change from one end or side to the other, especially in a game.
example: The teams swap ends at half-time.
usage: Swap ends is chiefly used in sports.

definition: Lamps powered by electricity.
example: Electric lamps lit the corridor after dark.

definition: The way letters are shaped when written or printed.
example: The worksheet practises letter formation for young learners.

definition: A farmer who operates a relatively small farm or area of land.
example: The cooperative provides tools and training for small-scale farmers.
